findings.reason: the §8 design should route the persisted profile through capabilities.cached_pick_input_stamped (one named input per project) or state why the existing cache cannot carry it, instead of standing up a second root and schema; the plan's own followup f-otmp-dispatch-prebuild already names capabilities.cached_pick_input as the intended cache owner.
findings.text: the persisted profile cache re-implements the cache its owner already provides: capabilities.pick_input_cache_root at reckon/capabilities.py:1143 and cached_pick_input_stamped at reckon/capabilities.py:1246 already resolve a root (RECKON_PICK_CACHE then RECKON_HOME then XDG_CACHE_HOME then ~/.cache), name an entry, and read/write it atomically with a version guard and error swallowing, which _profile_cache_root/_profile_cache_path/_profile_key/_read_persisted_profile/_write_persisted_profile here do again; the fork already cost once, when its own root precedence made two cases non-hermetic (recorded at the plan's own review c-run-r-20261003T050302383578)

findings.reason: the node should join on the backend's declared budget_group so the pace ruler reads one wallet per declared group, not one per name prefix.
findings.text: the codex pace reading joins a profile to a provider window by name prefix (name.startswith("codex")), which the grouping owner reckon/crew/budget_group.py forbids in its own docstring ("Grouping is read from resolved flight config — never inferred from a lane's name") and already serves through declared_groups and _declared_group_by_backend, so the §6 codex-pace node duplicates a decision the owner keeps a profile on

findings.reason: the sections adding crew pick and --route must name what of the absorbed routing options they fold in or replace, or why nothing can be, per the interface-budget rule.
findings.text: the plan introduces crew pick and its option set (--project --role --spec-level --goal --done-when --comment --estimated-context --capability --session --replay --outcomes --since --all-projects --checkout-path --pretty) plus dispatch's --route over routing.picker across §5/§8/§9 and the §6 measures, and while §1 names the three plans it absorbs conceptually and §11 names the 32 catalogue keys it merges, no section names a single CLI option or MCP view the new surface retires or merges, or says why none can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — pick() at reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:47 hides the ledger read, budget view, candidate enumeration, state rendering, Jev call, answer validation and fallback behind one pick(request, config, *, repo) call, and the package's eight modules split by concern rather than nesting shallow wrappers over one another.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py re-implements the cross-process picker-input cache that reckon/capabilities.py already owns, and reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py joins codex profiles to provider windows by name prefix rather than through the declared budget_group owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the plan adds the crew pick verb (with --outcomes, --replay, --since, --all-projects) and dispatch's --route, and no section names what any of that retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §4 records a reuse map (node picker-reuse-map, 28 base-revision functions over 2,060 ledger rows) and the built picker adapts existing owners rather than rebuilding them: reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py calls routing._competence_verdict, budget.preflight, lane_document.read_lane_document and dispatch._dispatch_lane_gate, and reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py reuses run_time_profile.run_time_profile and local_lane_load.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the picker extends the dispatch path rather than wrapping it in a parallel layer (reckon/crew/dispatch.py imports dispatch_picker_selection and _attach_shadow_picker_selection), and §4 keeps every hard constraint in code with Jev supplying only the semantic judgment.
